Roles
MediumRole guide

Bot Lane (ADC)

The marksman: weak early, unstoppable late, and always the team's main damage.

You'll enjoy this role if…

  • You enjoy farming and slowly becoming the strongest player on the map.
  • You like dealing damage from a distance while dodging enemies.
  • You want to play with a partner (your support) in lane.
  • You're good at positioning and staying alive under pressure.

What this role does

Bot lane is played by two players: the ADC (attack damage carry) and the support. The ADC is usually a ranged marksman who farms carefully, scales with items, and deals steady, huge damage in late-game fights as long as they stay alive.

  • Farm as much as possible: you're the most item-dependent role.
  • Play the 2v2 lane with your support and win trades together.
  • Take dragons with your jungler, since bot lane is right next to the dragon pit.
  • Stay alive in fights and deal damage to whatever is in range.
  • Push lanes and take turrets: marksmen destroy structures fast.

Champion types

  • Hyper carries like Jinx, Vayne and Smolder are weaker early but become game-winning late.
  • Lane bullies like Draven and Caitlyn win the early game with high damage or long range and try to end the game fast.
  • Utility marksmen like Ashe and Jhin bring crowd control and long-range plays.
  • Skill-shot marksmen like Ezreal rely on abilities and poke from range.
  • Mages in bot like Ziggs also work well, pushing waves and destroying turrets.

We have full guides for every marksman named here: see the list at the bottom of this page.

The 2v2 lane

Bot lane is about teamwork. You and your support fight together against another pair.

  • Start: most marksmen start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion.
  • The level 2 race is huge in bot lane. You reach level 2 after the first wave plus three melee minions from the second wave. If you hit level 2 first, you and your support can attack while the enemy has only one ability.
  • Follow your support's engage. When your support lands a stun or hook, attack right away. Hesitating wastes their play.
  • Trade when the enemy support goes in. If the enemy support walks forward without protection, punish them.
  • Watch for ganks, especially when your wave is pushed. Ward the river and tri-brush.
Pro tipTalk to your support with pings. Ping "on my way" on an enemy when you want to fight, and "retreat" when you're low. Good duos often win lanes just by acting at the same time.

Your role quest

The bot lane quest needs 1350 points, mostly from farming, plates, takedowns and time in lane. The reward:

  • +300 gold right away.
  • +2 gold for every minion you kill afterward, and +40 gold per takedown.
  • Your boots move to the quest slot, freeing a whole item slot. That's effectively a seventh item late in the game.

This is why farming matters so much as an ADC: more minions finish your quest faster, and then each minion pays even more.

Kiting

Kiting means attacking while moving, so the enemy can't reach you. It's the most important mechanical skill for marksmen.

  1. Attack the enemy.
  2. As soon as the attack fires, click to move (away from a melee enemy, or toward a fleeing one).
  3. Attack again when your attack is ready.

Moving back between attacks is called kiting back. Moving forward between attacks to chase is kiting forward. Practice in the practice tool: attack a target dummy and move between every attack. Use "attack move" (an attack-move key binding) to attack the nearest enemy without accidentally walking into them.

Common mistakeDon't stand still while attacking in fights. A marksman who doesn't move is the easiest target for every enemy ability.

Positioning in fights

Late in the game, your team's chances depend on you staying alive and doing damage. The rule: attack the closest enemy you can hit safely.

  • Stand behind your frontline (tanks and fighters).
  • Know the enemy's threats: which assassin or diver will jump on you? Keep your Flash and escape for them.
  • Don't dive for the enemy carry if it means walking past three enemies. Hitting their tank from safety is better than dying.
  • Stay with your support. A good support protects you with shields, heals and crowd control.

Read Teamfighting Basics for more about roles in fights.

Mid and late game

After laning, ADCs often move to mid lane, where they can farm safely and join fights quickly. Keep farming waves: as a marksman, you need items to deal damage.

Group with your team for dragons and Baron. Never walk into the side lanes alone late in the game without vision: you're the enemy's favorite target to catch.

When your team takes Baron, use the buff to push turrets with your minions. Marksmen take down structures faster than anyone.

Advanced tips

  • Track the enemy jungler. When they're seen top side, your lane can play aggressively. See Tracking the Enemy Jungler.
  • Manage the wave for dragon. Push your wave before dragon spawns, so you get to the pit first. See Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron.
  • Learn your power spikes. Most marksmen spike hard at their first and second completed items. Fight then. See Power Spikes: Know When You're Strong.
  • Recall at good times. Bring back enough gold for a component, and crash the wave first so you lose fewer minions. See Recall Timing and Tempo.

Beginner-friendly champions

AsheSlows every target and has a huge stun arrow. Easy to learn and useful all game.
Miss FortuneStrong early damage and a game-winning area ultimate in fights.
CaitlynLongest attack range among marksmen. Great for learning to farm safely and bully lanes.
JinxSimple kit that teaches positioning. Becomes a monster in the late game.
EzrealVery safe with a blink. Teaches skill shots and poke.

Common mistakes

  • Walking up to farm when the enemy jungler might be nearby, with no wards.
  • Not following your support's engage, leaving them to die alone.
  • Standing in front of your team in fights.
  • Facechecking brushes in the late game.
  • Missing lots of minions: you need gold more than any other role.
  • Chasing kills too far and getting caught.
